item.title: Ep 5: Concurrency Models Compared — Swift vs Kotlin
item.description:
Swift's async/await and actors versus Kotlin's coroutines and Flow: where the two concurrency models genuinely agree, where they diverge — compiler-enforced isolation versus library-level discipline — and where concurrency bugs cluster on each platform, plus what coroutines look like in shared K M P code.

Chapters:

  • 0:00 Cold open
  • 1:25 Swift concurrency in one pass
  • 4:50 Actors, isolation, and Sendable
  • 8:25 Kotlin coroutines in one pass
  • 12:30 Shared mutable state — actors versus Mutex
  • 14:40 Streams — Flow versus AsyncSequence
  • 17:40 The main thread, both ways
  • 19:30 The K M P wrinkle
  • 21:45 Where bugs cluster — the review checklist
  • 24:35 Takeaway

item.title: Special: Koin Deep Dive
item.description:
Koin under the hood: the registry-and-resolver model, the definitions D S L (single, factory, scoped), qualifiers and parameters, scope lifetimes, the runtime-resolution trade-off and checkModules, Koin Annotations with K S P, organizing modules by feature and layer, the K M P graph split, the iOS bridge problem, testing the graph, and when to choose manual D I, Dagger, or kotlin-inject instead.

item.title: Ep 6: Modularization at Scale
item.description:
